Let me structure the technical content carefully.

## Core motivation

Autoregressive decoding is memory-bandwidth bound. Each token generation requires reading the full model weights (and KV cache) from HBM to compute one token. For a 70B model in FP16, that's 140GB of weight reads per token. The GPU's compute units are massively underutilized during decode — arithmetic intensity is ~1 FLOP per byte read, far below the roofline. So you can often verify multiple tokens for roughly the cost of one token (latency-wise), especially at small batch sizes where there's spare compute.

Key insight: use a cheap model (draft) to generate k candidate tokens quickly, then verify all k with the expensive target model in a single forward pass (since a single forward pass through a transformer produces logits for all positions in parallel — the KV cache means we can score tokens at positions t+1...t+k in one pass).

1. Draft model q generates k tokens autoregressively (small, fast, possibly n-gram or draft model).
